findings.title: Off-by-one bounds check allows out-of-bounds read in Ins_NPUSHB
findings.message: In `Ins_NPUSHB`, the bounds check `if ( IP + L > exc->codeSize )` uses strict greater-than (`>`) rather than greater-than-or-equal (`>=`). Because the code array is 0-indexed and valid indices span `0` to `codeSize - 1`, the condition permits `IP + L == codeSize`. The subsequent loop `args[K] = exc->code[++IP]` then increments IP up to `codeSize`, reading one byte past the end of the heap-allocated code buffer. AddressSanitizer confirms a READ of size 1 immediately after the 32-byte allocation boundary.
findings.suggestion: Replace all `>` comparisons with `>=` in the code-overflow checks for Ins_NPUSHB, Ins_NPUSHW, Ins_PUSHB, and Ins_PUSHW. Valid code array indices are 0..codeSize-1, so `IP + L >= codeSize` is required to prevent the final byte from being read at index `codeSize`.

ground_truth.root_cause: The introducing commit `c3a5513` refactored the PUSH instruction handlers to perform their own IP advance and bounds checking. The bounds check `IP + L > exc->codeSize` uses strict greater-than, but the code array is 0-indexed (size `codeSize`, indices 0..codeSize-1). When `IP + L` exactly equals `codeSize`, the check passes, and the subsequent byte-reading loop reaches `exc->code[codeSize]` — one byte past the allocation.
